findings.summary: Read-back capacity was smaller than publication capacity. artifact-binding put the artifact body on the wire as base64, so a read request grew to about 4/3 of the artifact while every operation shares one fixed 8 MiB input ceiling. An artifact that put() accepted could therefore be unreadable, and an already published, already referenced artifact could not be read back at all.
findings.user_visible_consequence: Completed work could not be resumed: a worker that had written its receipt could not read it back on re-entry.
findings.reproduction: 6.25 MiB artifact: put() succeeds, the pre-migration get() succeeds, M3's get() raises 'bridge input exceeds 8 MiB'; a real worker re-entry fails.

findings.observed: The unchanged workflow test returned from the graph without a terminal key and raised KeyError('terminal') at line 54, with no check-complete, evaluate or seal before it.

acceptance_attempt.blocker: ZCODE_TRANSPORT: Native output closed (doctor exit 2). The ZCode app-server exits immediately.
acceptance_attempt.blocker_cause: SEE CORRECTION. The cause is not the host install. Two parts, both on our side: (a) FIXED - ZCode 3.12.3 ships the app-server's built-in provider catalogue at <Resources>/config/provider/zcode-builtin.json, while the app-server only derives <script dir>/provider/zcode-builtin.json and a source-tree-relative ../../../../../config/provider/zcode-builtin.json (which normalises to /config/provider/zcode-builtin.json). Both miss, so it exits 1 before emitting any protocol. The file is present; only its location moved. (b) NOT FIXED - the same build removed workspace/readState, which this transport calls first, and session/create now answers settings.model={"available": []} with no current selection.

adaptation_applied.what: Two changes. (1) native_transport.py now owns what every native transport shares - spawning one host process, the line-delimited JSON request/reply loop, the routing-only trace, answering the host's own client-directed requests, error classification, bindings, the four evidence files and session close - and an adapter supplies protocol hooks only: ident/envelope, respond, classify, notification. native_dsh.py drops its own reader, request loop, process lifecycle and binding; native_zcode.py drops its framing. Both declare the shared module in TRANSPORT_FILES, so a fix to the shared mechanics stays reviewable as a transport change for every host. (2) The ZCode transport is adapted to the 3.12.3 surface: workspace/readState is no longer called, the snapshot comes straight from session/resume or session/create, the handshake every snapshot carries is checked instead of assumed, and selection is applied only through session/setModel with persistAsWorkspaceLastUsed:false and confirmed from the host's own report. The transport no longer assembles a provider runtime config for the host.
adaptation_applied.verified: go vet exit 0. Python suite 206 OK (199 before; +3 host-side, +4 shared-boundary). doctor --provider dsh PASSES end to end through the shared boundary, so extracting it did not change DSH behaviour. doctor --provider zcode still fails, but at a different point - see remaining_adaptation.

The session is created, the ZCode Protocol v1 handshake passes and the settings snapshot is read; the host itself reports no selected model.

remaining_adaptation.what: The app-server this adapter spawns has no provider runtime context: session/create reports settings.model={"current": null, "available": []} and every provider reference is refused with -32603, so the transport refuses rather than inventing a selection (ZCODE_CONFIG: native selected model missing). This is NOT the machine having no provider: the ZCode desktop host's own log records its provider runtime with providerCount: 2 for the same app and the same account, and its entitlement line names preferredProviderId account:bigmodel-individual-coding-plan.
remaining_adaptation.judged_not_assumed: Measured, not inferred. (1) The desktop host has providers, we do not: ~/.zcode/v2/logs/2026-09-18.log carries the desktop's spawn preflight (command "ZCode Helper", args [zcode.cjs, app-server, --stdio, --surface, desktop], cwd = workspace) and, from the same process, [provider-runtime] {"configRevision":"[zcode-builtin:28:a7b54955...,2915b997...]","providerCount":2}. Every launch this adapter makes writes zcode_protocol.provider_registry.ready with providerCount: 0 (44 events in ~/.zcode/cli/log/zcode-2026-09-18.jsonl, none above 0). The two built-in revision hashes differ (a7b54955... on the desktop side, c1a2fc01... for us). (2) The desktop's executable and argv do not reproduce it: spawning with the "ZCode Helper" binary instead of node, and with "app-server --stdio --surface desktop" instead of "--cwd WS app-server", still reports available: 0 (desktop-contract.py, variants A-D; without a named catalogue the Helper exits on the host's own catalogue lookup, exactly as node does). (3) The authority-mode variable does not reproduce it either: ZCODE_SERVICE_AUTHORITY_MODE, whose values are desktop-local / desktop-attached-remote / standalone-server and which selects the registry source (shouldUseProviderRegistrySourceForAuthorityMode is false only for desktop-attached-remote), gives available: 0 in all three values (authority-mode.py). (4) Rule sources are empty on the file level while the desktop still has 2 providers: the built-in release (revision 28) contributes 20 templateRules and 8 providerRules that are all account:*, with no builtin:* rule, and the only personal provider document has providerRules: []. So the 2 providers the desktop host reports are resolved at run time from account/authorization context, not read from these files. (5) Withdrawn from the earlier rounds: the claim that "every launcher input was measured and excluded" was false (the --surface flag, the Helper executable and the authority-mode variable had never been tried), and the claim that "this host has no selectable provider" is false - the desktop host has 2 for the same account.
remaining_adaptation.what_is_empty: Not the user's provider configuration, as the earlier rounds concluded. The files are empty on purpose at the file level: the built-in release contributes only 20 templateRules plus 8 account:* providerRules (entitlement-gated) and the personal provider document has 0 rules. The desktop host nevertheless reports 2 providers for the same account, so the selectable set is resolved at run time from account/authorization context the desktop supplies when it spawns the agent. What this transport lacks is that handoff, not a file to populate; populating files is what the earlier positive controls tried and why they could not construct a non-empty registry.
remaining_adaptation.impact: doctor-zcode is one of the nine required items for EVERY unit, so no unit can close while it fails. The failure is "an unattended spawn does not receive the provider runtime context the desktop client supplies", not "our protocol assumption is stale" and not "the user has no usable plan" - the plan is usable, as the desktop proves. Whether an unattended acceptance can obtain that context at all is a plan-level question (section 12.4 delivers native interaction separately).
remaining_adaptation.determination: Corrected. This is not host account state and not an absent subscription: the desktop host reports providerCount: 2 and resolves the BigModel entitlement for account:bigmodel-individual-coding-plan, while every unattended launch this adapter can construct reports providerCount: 0. The provider runtime context is handed to the agent by the desktop at launch time and is absent from disk, from argv, and from the environment names the bundle exposes; the desktop executable, its argv and the authority-mode variable were each measured this round and none of them reproduces it. What remains unverified is the exact handoff (a live agent process environment could not be read: process inspection is refused in this sandbox). Disposition per plan section 12.5: doctor-zcode is a required item for every unit and the native verification is still blocked, so the M3 repair candidate stays unaccepted, G1b and G2a must not close on it, and no code change is made this round - naming an env var or an argv that measures equal would be churn. The open question this raises is a plan-level one: an unattended acceptance cannot obtain a context only the desktop client supplies, which is the class of thing section 12.4 delivers separately as native interaction.
